svg.text: Example: Anna writes, an agent answers, a colleague pushes
Team wiki as a Git source with a push webhook · Tom has the note open · Lena follows the folder (e-mail “bundled”) · an agent listens via event webhook
👩 Anna types a paragraph in “Project plan” and stops.
in the browser
📄 Saved – the file on the server is new.
👨 Tom sees the paragraph at once in his open note (his cursor stays where it was).
🔵 Lena gets a dot in the tree at once.
⚡ Event webhook: the agent gets “Project plan changed, by Anna”.
Kaveyl Wiki bundles what happens within one second, then calls the address of the agent.
🤖 The agent writes its answer into the note via MCP – Anna and Tom see it at once.
How long the agent takes depends on the agent. The webhook does not report its own change back to it.
✉️ Lena gets one e-mail with both changes (Anna and the agent).
“Bundled” = 2 minutes after the first change. With “hourly” or “daily” it would come later.
⬆ 2-minute pause: commit + push to Gitea – one commit for Anna, one for the agent.
Had Anna left the note or pressed Ctrl+S, this would have happened at 10:00 already.
If someone writes on without a pause, Kaveyl Wiki sends at least every 10 minutes.
🧑‍💻 The colleague changes the same note in VS Code and runs git push.
She works in her own copy of the repository; first she fetches the 10:02 state with git pull.
⚡ Gitea reports the push via webhook – Kaveyl Wiki fetches the change at once.
👨 Tom and 👩 Anna see it in the open note, 🔵 Lena gets a dot,
⚡ the agent its event webhook (“from outside”), and ✉️ Lena’s next e-mail follows 2 minutes later.
Without a push webhook this happens at the next sync – within 5 minutes (here by 10:08).
In short
Inside Kaveyl Wiki (app, API, MCP) everything is there at once – for everyone allowed to see it.
To Git it goes in batches: leave the note / Ctrl+S at once, else after the pause (default 2 min, per source), at least every 10 min.
From Git it comes every 5 minutes – with a push webhook after ~1 second. Event webhooks pass on every change after ~1 second.
